title: Module 36: Equity Jurisdictions, Classes, and the Voting Process
module_name: Equity Jurisdictions, Classes, and the Voting Process

prompt.text: Which type of DR would MSUMC most likely own?

choices:
Either type of DR
Feedback
Choice B is correct. MSUMC would prefer to own sponsored DRs because the holder of sponsored receipts 
retains shareholder voting rights.
Choices A and C are incorrect because the depository bank retains the voting rights on the company’s shares 
in an unsponsored DR.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text:
Which one of the following statements provides the most likely reason why MSUMC would place a ban on 
owning shares of companies with dual class structures?

choices: Dual class structures typically provide multiple classes of traded shares with unequal voting rights.
Dual class structures typically provide unequal cash flow rights to shareholders.

Dual class structures typically provide one class of untraded shares with superior voting rights to those 
of traded shares.
Feedback
Correct Answer: C. Dual class structures typically provide one class of untraded shares with superior voting 
rights to those of traded shares.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text:
Which one of the following conditions would most likely be necessary for MSUMC to vote “yes” on a 
shareholder proposal that would cause the board to encroach on day-to-day management?

choices:
Management presents arguments in the proxy statement that the risk mitigation of the proposal is not 
material.
Management is already working on the issue underlying the proposal.

Management following the proposal would materially improve firm value
Feedback
Choice C is correct. In general, a shareholder proposal that, if passed, would cause the board to encroach on 
management’s day-to-day operations is not appropriate unless the actions would have material and positive 
effects on firm value and/or risk mitigation.
Choice A is incorrect because MSUMC is unlikely to base their vote on management’s arguments.
Choice B is incorrect as this is typically likely to result in a “no” vote by MSUMC.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text: Which of the following are typically correct about management and shareholder proposals?

choices: Both proposal types are shown in the company’s proxy statement.
Shareholder proposals are binding if passed.

Shareholder proposals are frequently passed
Feedback
Choice A is correct. A company’s proxy statement includes both management and shareholder proposals, 
including the company’s voting recommendations to shareholders along with the rationales for the 
recommendations.
Choice B is incorrect because shareholder proposals, if passed, are typically not binding on the company.
Choice C is incorrect because shareholder proposals are not frequently passed.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text: The voting rights of an unsponsored depository receipt (DR) belong to the:

choices: direct owners of the foreign common shares.

foreign company whose shares are held by the depository.
Feedback: 
A is correct. In the case of unsponsored DRs, the depository bank, not the investors in the DR, retains the 
voting rights.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.
